_doc: Director motion data (rr-48), humanoid rig v2 for the Ashen Reaver on the mq-23 maquette and the owner-approved take-two paintings (inbox reaver-paint-3, 2026-10-28). Same binding semantics as rr-38/rr-44 (held item, angle_deg, release_at, drop), rr-29 (shoulder_pendulum) and the rig spec. falchion.angle_deg rotates the falchion about its grip in the facing plane: positive lifts the point up toward the head, negative drives it down toward the floor; 0 is the painted rest (held low and forward, point down and out).

art.registration_note: The paintings are about 25% bulkier than the maquette (director check, 2026-10-28). Register joints on the paintings themselves, guided by the maquette's part map; never by bounding-box mapping of maquette joints.

ashen_reaver.pieces_note: head = the angular crested great helm with the cross visor (front only), rigid; torso with the leather cowl, scarf, cross strap, round bronze buckle and BOTH pauldrons fused in (rigid; the pauldrons sit over the shoulder joints, so no pauldron pixel may belong to an arm: the arms swing beneath them); pelvis with the broad belt and square buckle fused in; loincloth = the deep-red front loincloth (front view) as a skinned cloth chain on pelvis (loincloth_mid, loincloth_tip; at most 3 px follow-through); loincloth_back = the back loincloth (rear view; its hem also shows between the legs in the front) as a skinned cloth chain on pelvis (loincloth_back_mid, loincloth_back_tip; at most 3 px follow-through); per arm a skinned root limb over upper and fore with the plate gauntlet as a rigid hand; falchion = the curved blade, crossguard, leather-wrapped grip and pommel as one rigid held item in hand_far (the sword hand is the far hand in the front and the near-camera right hand in the rear; follow the maquette's part labels, which name it hand_far in both views), pivot at the grip; per leg a skinned root leg (cuisse, knee cop with its side wing, greave) and a rigid sabaton. Hidden fills (spec 1, the rr-37/rr-42/rr-44 lesson): every area a moving arm, gauntlet, falchion or loincloth uncovers must show its covered piece's own painted continuation (torso flanks and belly under each arm's full motion footprint, the front loincloth and thighs under the near gauntlet, the far thigh and flank under the falchion arm). Report those regions as masks; the director paints the underlays.

elbow_policy._doc: As rr-44 (owner 2026-10-27): a real elbow only flexes; the forearm folds from the upper arm's line toward the side the figure faces. The two-bone solve always takes this side and never infers it from a near-straight rest. 'max_hyperextension_deg' is the gate.

idle.note: the protagonist's cut-out bob: the upper body drops 2 px and returns as one rigid piece; the falchion arm follows a beat later as one rigid group with the blade (the Thrall's pre-computed sword-lag curve on upper_far); the free fist, loincloths, legs and feet stay still

move.note: a heavy armoured advance on the protagonist's model, from the fighter's crouch: both legs step, six steps per tile, near foot leading, a 5 px lift; a 4 degree forward lean; both arms swing from the shoulder like pendulums, opposite their same-side legs, the forearm trailing; the sword arm swings less and the falchion trails the fist (held_follow); the loincloths trail 2 px

arm_swing._doc: As rr-44: the upper arm rotates about the shoulder toward the facing and away from it, opposite the same-side leg; the forearm follows with a lag and bends more on the backswing; the hand is rigid with the forearm. The falchion arm swings less.

held_follow._doc: The blade trails the swinging fist: falchion.angle_deg(t) = deg_per_px x (the grip's displacement along the facing, in source px, from its rest position, at t - lag_s; 0 before the clip starts). The fist swinging forward tips the point back and up a little.

rake.note: after the step in (the move clip), he drags the falchion's burning edge along the ground ahead: the blade lifts and draws back a little, then the sword arm drives forward and down so the point scrapes the floor in front of him (contact: the fire line starts here) and keeps dragging forward through 0.7, the body leaning in and the hips dropping into the crouch; then he rises back to the guard. The free fist pulls back for balance; its elbow only flexes (elbow_policy).
rake.budget_note: Director targets: if a value exceeds the measured joint budget for that limb (no tear, no exposed unpainted texel), clamp it to the budget and report the clamp (rr-38 feedback 1).

sweep.note: after the step in, a wide hooked sweep: the falchion is drawn back and up across his shoulder with a lean back (wind-up), then swung through the whole front arc at waist height (contact: the hit, the fire and the push land here), following through low on the far side with the body turned into it; held a beat, then back to the guard. The free fist swings opposite for balance.
sweep.budget_note: Director targets: if a value exceeds the measured joint budget for that limb (no tear, no exposed unpainted texel), clamp it to the budget and report the clamp (rr-38 feedback 1).

fall.note: after the step in, the executioner's chop: he raises the falchion to shoulder height with the point up and back over his shoulder, leaning back (0.3), then brings it down hard in front of him so the blade strikes the floor ahead (contact: the fire line runs out from here), the body folded over it and the hips low; he stays bent over the planted blade through 0.85, open to a counter-attack (the move leaves him exposed), then heaves himself back up to the guard. The free fist pulls back to the hip through the chop.
fall.budget_note: Director targets: if a value exceeds the measured joint budget for that limb (no tear, no exposed unpainted texel), clamp it to the budget and report the clamp (rr-38 feedback 1).

hit.note: spec hit: torso knocked 3 px back and 1 px down with a 3 degree lean back, the helm nods back 4 degrees; both hands carry the knockback a beat late (the arms hang loose and catch up), so the elbows only flex; the falchion's point dips 6 degrees as the body is knocked back, then settles; the loincloths flick 2 px; recovered by 0.6

death.note: staggers back; the falchion slips from his grip at 0.3, drops straight to the floor under the fist and tips over to lie flat along the floor (the Gaoler's chain-drop model: the owner loved the weapon falling); the body slumps forward over planted feet (hips sink 6 px, torso folds 24 degrees, helm bowed 18 degrees), no kneel: plate legs cannot fold that far without tearing; both arms hang limp as the body folds; the loincloths settle; terminal pose held, then the existing fade

falchion.drop.note: as rr-44's chain.drop: translate straight down from release until the falchion's lowest texel touches the unit's floor line (measured per facing from the rig), then falchion.angle_deg pivots about the floor contact so the blade lies flat

death.budget_note: slump instead of a kneel (director decision, as rr-42); Director targets: if a value exceeds the measured joint budget for that limb (no tear, no exposed unpainted texel), clamp it to the budget and report the clamp (rr-38 feedback 1).
